div.head: Real-time system should guarantee that each hard real-time task completes execution before its deadline. When non-preemptive Earliest Deadline First(EDF) scheduling is used for a set of periodic tasks, one can achieve full processor utilization, but its schedulability test is known to be an NP-hard problem. Continuous media(CM) retrieval is becoming an important application of real-time system. In such application, the CM server should provide CM data requested by clients within the specified deadline. In this paper, we examine the O(1) time on-line schedulability tests for a set of equal computation time task and for a set of equal period tasks using non-preemptive EDF algorithm.
div.p: We also demonsnare that these results can be used for scheduling a set of client requests in CM retrieval system.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: The scheduling of periodic tasks with hard deadlines is an important problem in real-time systems. In the case of permitting task preemption, one representative scheduling method is Rate M o n o t o n i c 0 theory [l]. RM provides the simple schedulability test based on the processor utilization factor, i.e., the fraction of processor time spent in the execution of the task set. Many works have successively weakened the constraints of RM approach [7][11]. Earliest Deadline Fmt(EDF) scheduling is another popular method also proposed by Liu [l]. EDF scheduling assigns priorities to tasks dynamically. The task with earliest deadline gains the highest priority. Many analytic studies on EDF have been reported [3] [4].

In contrast, relatively few studies have been conducted for the case of non-preemptive scheduling. Many non-preemptive scheduling problems have been shown to be NP-hard [Z]. So, many works have focused on more restrictive problems for which efficient Algorithms are available. Non-preemptive scheduling is important for the following reasons [5]:
Many real-time scheduling problems involve Yo traffic between various devices, which does not allow to preempt by nature.

Non-preemptive scheduling on a uniprocessor system naturally guarantees exclusive access to shared resources and data. So, no synchronization effort such as Priority Inheritance Protocol [9], is needed.

The overhead of preemptive algorithm is m m difficult to characterize and predict than nonpreemptive algorithm because of its ignoring preemption and resumption overhead. So, nonpreemptive scheduling can exhibit lower runtime overhead.

Continuous media(CM) means the data requested by users with timing requirements, for example, digital audio and motion video. We consider the problem of providing CM data to the interactive users. We assume the system is a multi-user, client-server system [l][lO].

In such CM retrieval system, the CM server must transfer data from the data repositoryhard disk, optical disk, network media, etc.to the clients satisfying the given timing requirements. For example, the CM server should provide the next block of CM data to a client before the current data block in the client side is used up. So, such requests of clients naturally contain the real-time scheduling problem.

The following section presents our system model in detail. Section 3 reviews related literature on EDF scheduling. Section 4 demonstrates that 0(1) nonpreemptive EDF schedulability tests with full processor utilization are possible for a set of tasks with restricted timing constraints that are allowable in CM retrieval systems. Section 5 discusses these results.

As described above, we focus on the problem of scheduling U0 requests in CM retrieval systems. In this system, there are one CM server and many clients that request CM data. When CM server receives the request of a client, if the server can supply CM data to the client within requested deadline then the session betwen the client and the CM server is established and bounded buffer space is allocated for each session. For example, a client CP, requests CM data with data rate D,, i.e., the number of data blocks per one second playback and each session has bounded buffer space E, (Figure 1). To guarantee smooth CM presentation, CM server should transfer E, data blocks to the buffer of the client CP, at every T, second, where T,=BJD,, if E , is the allocated buffer size in terms of the data block size.
So, we can regard this system as a problem of real-time scheduling for a set of periodic tasks.

Without any assumptions on disk layout, disk driver can guarantee only one block transfer time. In network media, only a packet transfer time can be guaranteed at most. In these cases, we consider such a predictable unit transfer time as equal computation time of all tasks in real-time scheduling. Many works on continuous media f i e system assume that all data blocks requested by a client are contiguous in disk. The maximum performance can be obtained by setting all periods equal in this situation.

In this paper, we show that for a set of tasks with equal computation time, when both the period and the release time of each task are integral multiple of computation time, it is schedulable under nonpreemptive EDF with full processor utilization. We will also show that for a set of equal period tasks, it is schedulable using non-preemptive EDF if the sum of computation times of tasks is less than or equal to the period of task.

div.head: Related Works
div.p: Liu and Layland developed EDF and have shown that (1) is the necessary and sufficient condition for EDF scheduling when task preemption is permitted [8]. In non-preemptive EDF scheduling, a set of tasks can overrun though its processor utilization factor does not exceed 1.

T" In uniprocessor system, non-preemptive schedulability test for a set of periodic task is known to be NP-hard [2]. Recent research of Jeffiy [S] demonstrated the intractability of deciding schedulabiiity for an even simpler characterbation of periodic tasks. Time complexity of the scheddability test is pseudo-polynomial time for a set of periodic tasks with arbitrary release time. But, the problem of deciding if a set of periodic tasks with specified deadline is schedulable under any non-preemptive scheduling algorithm is NP-hard in the strong sense. Non-preemptive FDF scheduling for the restricted set of periodic tasks has been considered in [6]-In this work, two periodic tasks are schedulable with nonpreemptive EDF if and only if the sum of the computation times of two tasks do not exceed the shorter period of two tasks. For a set of n periodic tasks with equal computation time(C), there is no task overrun if the processor utilization factor is less than or equal to l-C/Tl, where T, is the shortest period among the set of tasks.

Integral means exactly integral multiple of computation time. Next, we consider the case of equal period tasks.

div.head: A Set of Equal Period tasks
div.p: We consider a set of tasks with equal period and arbitrary computation time. Following theorem gives the universal condition for non-preemptive scheduling of equal period tasks.

Clearly, there is no processor idle time during this period. In this case, the tasks with deadliie later than T could not be executed because all periods are equal. This theorem tells that if the sum of the computation time of tasks in a set does not exceed the length of equal period, the task set is schedulable under non-preemptive EDF with no additional restrictions. Illustrated example is successful non-preemptive EDF scheduling when all periods of tasks are equal.

div.head: Discussion
div.p: This study has some restrictions on scheduling a set of equal computation time tasks. F i t , every period of task must be integral multiple of computation time. T h i s t x " ' t can be fulfilled simply by adjusting period of each task as p =c.LgJ.

Adjusted period is always shorter than or equal to the original period. In CM retrieval systems, it implies that the number of data blocks supplied in a time interval can be incmsd than quested. So, it quires some more buffer space for stming over-supplied data block, but the timing requirements of a client cannot be affected at all. Analysis on the buffer space is not the scope of this paper. It will be consided in following papas on the file systems for CM retrieval.

Second restriction is that the release time of each task must be at integral multiple of computation time. It is natural to hold the release of a client during the transfer for anothex client on single server system. If it is on server idle time, a client waits a half of a block transfer time in average. In CM retrieval system, it is possible that the CM server delays session establishment as much as necessary. So, this constraint can be permitted. When the interactions between clients are allowed, more precise studies on the client synchronization problems are needed.
For equal period tasks, there is no restrictions on their periods and release times.

On-line schedulability test proposed in this paper has O(1) time complexity for each request to create session between a client and server regardless of disk layout. It merely compares the newly requested data rate of a client with the remaining service capacity of CM server.

div.head: Summary
div.p: This paper shows that for a set of tasks with equal computation time, when their periods and release times are exactly integral multiple of computation time, nonpreemptive EDF scheduling which fully utilizes the processor capacity is possible, and the on-line schedulability test for the set of tasks is performed with O(1) time complexity. We also show that for a set of equal period tasks with no additional restriction, full processor utilization can be achieved using nonpreemptive EDF scheduling. On-line schedulability test for this set of tasks has also O(1) time complexity. And we demonstrate that these results can be used for scheduling I/O traffic between clients and server in CM retrieval systems.
